messages.subject_clean: Bootcamps 2014: Call for participation / declarations of interest
messages.body_plain:
* B o o t c a m p s   2 0 1 4 *

This year, there will definitely be a 4-day bootcamp on statistics for linguists with R (starting from relatively scratch but then aiming to focus on regression modeling) at the University of Mississippi, Oxford (4-7 August 2014). If you're interested in taking that bootcamp, plz contact Chris Sapp (<http://home.olemiss.edu/~csapp/ <http://home.olemiss.edu/%7Ecsapp/>>).

In addition, Stefanie Wulff and I are in the process of preparing
- a five-day bootcamp on corpus linguistics with R (frequency lists, concordancing, etc.) at UCSB (11-15 or 16 August 2014);
- a five-day bootcamp on statistics for linguistics with R (introduction, mono- and multifactorial tests, and regression modeling) at UCSB (18-22 or 23 August 2014).
While our preparation has not been finalized yet, we're optimistic we can make it happen so if you think you'd be interested in taking one or both of these, plz contact Stefanie Wulff (<http://www.clas.ufl.edu/users/swulff/>) to be put on a priority list.

STG
--
Stefan Th. Gries
-----------------------------------------------
University of California, Santa Barbara
http://www.linguistics.ucsb.edu/faculty/stgries
-----------------------------------------------

messages.subject: Seeing whether a word + pattern association is stronger in one corpus compared to another
messages.subject_clean: Seeing whether a word + pattern association is stronger in one corpus compared to another
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

Sorry for what may be a novice-level CL/stats question. This has less to do with R and more with corpus analysis generally.

I'm interested in getting the association strength between particular words and specific patterns in three sub-corpora (e.g., NOUNS that occur in the pattern the N of). That is, I want to find the likelihood that there is indeed an attraction between a word & pattern.

Attempting to follow methods in publications, I wanted to do this by applying a Fischer Exact test within each sub-corpus. I can then observe how these words associate with the patterns in rank order within each corpus.

But what can I do next to find out if the word/pattern associations are stronger or weaker in one sub-corpus compared to the other sub-corpora? Is it just a matter of visually observing differences in the p log values in each corpus or is there a statistical test I could do to show the degree to which the corpora differ in how strongly a particular word associates with a pattern?

Apologies too if my wording is unclear, and thanks in advance for your thoughts!
Brian

messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] Seeing whether a word + pattern association is stronger in one corpus compared to another
messages.subject_clean: [CorpLing with R] Seeing whether a word + pattern association is stronger in one corpus compared to another
messages.body_plain:
In order to compare different corpora, I would not recommend using any
measure based on a significance test (such as the chi-squared test or
Fisher-Yates exact test) because those results would be affected by
both the effect size (which you're interested in) and the sample sizes
(which you're interested in). What you could use instead, for example,
is the odds ratio or Cramer's V, which by definition will not reflect
sample sizes.

HTH,
STG
--
Stefan Th. Gries
----------------------------------
Univ. of California, Santa Barbara
http://tinyurl.com/stgries
----------------------------------
